title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Ten documented JMU study settings spanning quiet solo booths, configurable work areas, reservable collaboration rooms, computer labs, and informal library seating.

cards.title: Settle In Around the Clock
cards.subtitle: Secure study space inside Rose Library
cards.notes: Bring your JACard and enter through Rose Library’s side door; choose among large tables, group rooms, computers, and soft seating.
cards.short_summary: A credentialed, always-open workspace with varied seating and essential study equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU identifies this as a 24-hour study space with tables, soft seating, group rooms, a computer and printing lab, vending machines, and JACard-controlled entry.
cards.access_notes: Available at any hour through the Rose Library side entrance; entry requires a JACard.

cards.title: Work With a Little Background Buzz
cards.subtitle: First-floor tables near Starbucks in Rose Library
cards.notes: Use a café-area table for casual reading or a short meetup when conversation and normal food-service noise will not disrupt your work.
cards.short_summary: An informal first-floor option suited to lighter assignments and brief collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU describes the tables near Starbucks in Rose Library as a café space for casual studying or short meetups.
cards.access_notes: Located on Rose Library’s first floor near Starbucks; use is subject to current library building hours.

cards.title: Build Breaks Into the Session
cards.subtitle: Second-floor study-and-break area in Rose Library
cards.notes: Pair coursework with a planned reset using the magazines, games, and LEGO bricks available in this second-floor Rose Library space.
cards.short_summary: A study setting with built-in materials for short, screen-free breaks.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU documents a second-floor Rose Library hangout space containing magazines, games, and LEGO bricks.
cards.access_notes: Located on Rose Library’s second floor and available during current library building hours.

cards.title: Put the Project on the Whiteboard
cards.subtitle: Reservable and walk-in collaboration rooms
cards.notes: Reserve a second- or fourth-floor room for a group session, or check first- and third-floor rooms that operate first come, first served.
cards.short_summary: Enclosed collaboration rooms with tables, whiteboards, and presentation options.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU says Rose Library has reservable group rooms on floors two and four and first-come, first-served rooms on floors one and three; rooms have large tables and whiteboards, and some include TVs.
cards.access_notes: Rooms are for groups of at least two; reservations are limited to two hours daily and may be made up to one week ahead.

cards.title: Reconfigure the Room Around the Task
cards.subtitle: Mobile furniture on Rose Library’s third floor
cards.notes: Roll the tables, chairs, and whiteboards into a layout that fits your group, then restore an orderly arrangement when the session ends.
cards.short_summary: A configurable work zone for assignments that benefit from movable surfaces and seating.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU identifies the third-floor Flex Space as an open area furnished with mobile chairs, tables, and whiteboards.
cards.access_notes: Located on Rose Library’s third floor and available during current library building hours.

cards.title: Close the Door on Distraction
cards.subtitle: Sound-dampened booths on Rose Library’s third floor
cards.notes: Choose a booth for focused solo work, then adjust the desk to your preferred position and keep conversation for a collaborative area.
cards.short_summary: Enclosed individual booths designed for concentrated, low-noise work.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU documents third-floor quiet booths with sound-dampening walls, individual airflow systems, and adjustable desks.
cards.access_notes: Located on Rose Library’s third floor; availability is subject to current library building hours and booth occupancy.

cards.title: Spread Out Above the Campus View
cards.subtitle: A tucked-away third-floor room in Rose Library
cards.notes: Exit the third-floor elevator, turn right, and continue to The Nook; use its large tables for materials that need room to spread out.
cards.short_summary: A smaller destination combining broad worktables with elevated campus views.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU identifies The Nook as a small third-floor Rose Library space with campus views, big tables, and usually one or two whiteboards.
cards.access_notes: From Rose Library’s third-floor elevator, turn right and continue to the room; use is subject to building hours.

cards.title: Take Notes Beside the Windows
cards.subtitle: Fifth-floor lounge overlooking East Campus
cards.notes: Head to Rose Library’s fifth floor for a window-side session; choose this lounge when natural light and an East Campus view fit the task.
cards.short_summary: An upper-floor lounge pairing casual study seating with expansive exterior views.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU’s study-spaces guide identifies the Balcony Lounge as a fifth-floor Rose Library study location with large windows and East Campus views.
cards.access_notes: Located on Rose Library’s fifth floor and available during current library building hours.

cards.title: Combine Desk Work With Computer Time
cards.subtitle: Open workspace in Memorial Hall’s ETMC
cards.notes: Use the desks, soft seating, or computer workstations for coursework; bring JMU credentials if your session requires a workstation login.
cards.short_summary: A Memorial Hall workspace offering several seating modes alongside desktop computers.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU states that the ETMC open study space has soft seating, desks, and computer workstations available to anyone with JMU credentials.
cards.access_notes: Find the ETMC on the second floor at the back of Memorial Hall; JMU credentials are required for computer workstations.

cards.title: Move From Research to Media Work
cards.subtitle: Mac-equipped lab inside the Music Library
cards.notes: Use a Mac workstation for regular study or music-technology work; find the lab in the Music Library on the Music Building’s basement level.
cards.short_summary: A technology-rich study lab that supports both ordinary coursework and media projects.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU identifies MusiCommons as the Music Library’s media and computer lab, equipped with 20 Mac workstations and available for regular study.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Music Library on the Music Building’s basement level; workstation access is subject to current library hours.
